established-precondition-contract-01.graded_text: The new row update requires a precondition from the caller (If-Match with the document's ETag, or a row-level equivalent) and answers a stale one with 412, matching the existing PUT contract.

votes.e: A/project/docs/row-updates.md:48 "`If-Match: <row ETag>` is required." and :57 "| `412` | `If-Match` does not match the current row ETag | `code: \"row_precondition_failed\"` ..."; :18 "A row `PUT` requires `If-Match` with the **row** ETag". This is the row-level equivalent of the PUT contract, it answers a stale precondition with 412, and :58 answers a missing one with 428. Row ETags come from GET .../rows/{rowId} (:40).

established-precondition-contract-02.graded_text: The existing PUT and its required If-Match stay unchanged.

votes.e: A/project/docs/row-updates.md:69 "| Whole-document `PUT` | Document ETag (unchanged contract) | ... | Changes |" and :19 "A partner still holding the old document ETag gets the existing `412` on their next whole-document `PUT`, so the published contract keeps protecting them"; :11 "must not change how existing calls behave". The required If-Match and the 412 stay as they are, and there is no code diff (A/diff.txt adds only docs/row-updates.md). The closest the design comes to breaking this is :32: whole-document PUT gains a new rejection, "An `id` that does not belong to this list is rejected with `422` and `code: \"unknown_row_id\"`". That extends the body semantics but leaves the precondition alone, and it only bites clients that send an `id` (see minor).

blocking: [claude-fallback] Under the brief's stated traffic, row ids churn and the per-row conflict model falls apart. A/project/docs/row-updates.md:31 says "A row with no `id` is new and gets a fresh one" and :33 says "A row that is left out is deleted". docs/brief.md says many partners "sync price lists unattended every few minutes", and :34 admits clients that rebuild the document "without echoing `id` ... rows just get new ids on each `PUT`". So each such sync deletes and re-mints every row id, and every other partner and every staff browser session holding a row id gets 404 row_not_found. This contradicts the design's own guarantees at :73 "Two partners edit different rows. Both succeed." and :76 "If that row's content did not change, the row `PUT` still succeeds." No lost update follows, but the feature built as written would fail routinely for exactly the concurrent-editing case it was meant to serve. The design has no fallback, such as matching rows without an id on unchanged content or a natural key.
